Predict and simulate robust longitudinal networks

Source: R/lame_robust_methods.R
predict.lame_robust.Rd

Posterior means and joint draws from a lame_robust() fit. Prediction uses the conditional mean; simulation also includes observation noise with the persistent directed-pair precision from the same posterior iteration.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'lame_robust'
predict(
  object,
  h = 0L,
  newdata = NULL,
  type = c("response", "link"),
  by_draw = FALSE,
  nsim = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'lame_robust'
simulate(object, nsim = 1L, seed = NULL, h = 0L, newdata = NULL, ...)

Arguments

object

A lame_robust fit.

h

Nonnegative integer forecast horizon. Zero returns observed periods.

newdata

For a positive horizon with covariates, a list of one dyadic design array per future period. For one period, a matrix or array is also accepted. Actor and covariate names are aligned to the fit. All future covariates must be supplied and finite off the diagonal. Omit otherwise.

type

Either "response" or "link"; both denote the continuous mean.

by_draw

Logical; return joint posterior mean-network draws. Forecast draws include future latent innovations. The default posterior mean integrates those innovations analytically before averaging over draws.

nsim

Number of posterior draws. NULL uses every retained iteration. Simulation defaults to one. Smaller requests sample without replacement; larger requests sample with replacement. Selected indices are sorted.

seed

Optional seed preserving the caller's RNG state.

...

No additional arguments are supported.

Value

Prediction returns a sender-by-receiver-by-period array, or a sender-by-receiver-by-period-by-draw array when by_draw = TRUE. Simulation always returns the four-dimensional form. Diagonals are NA. Draw arrays carry a draw_index attribute identifying the joint posterior iteration. Singleton dimensions are preserved.

Details

Future intercepts, actor deviations, and factors follow their sampled AR(1) laws. Actor innovations respect the sum-to-zero constraints. Finite actor_df draws a new precision for each actor role and forecast period. Persistent actor levels and pair precisions remain the same within each simulated trajectory. Simulation at h = 0 replicates observations conditional on the saved mean paths and persistent pair scales. Finite observation_df draws fresh temporary residual precisions for every replicated observation, including at h = 0; fitted observation precisions are not reused. Simulation at a positive horizon draws both future states and observation noise. Future latent uncertainty is included when by_draw = TRUE; its Monte Carlo average need not equal the analytically integrated default point forecast exactly.
